terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A new project-owned tank mount inspired by the supplied multi-view concept. The source name, tower crest, lettering, and exact heraldry are deliberately omitted. The hidden rear and underside are inferred from the admitted side and front views.

reasoning: The identity depends on a squat wide hull, twin track pods, a compact saddle turret, and a deliberately oversized stepped cannon.
Five visible road wheels per side, segmented tracks, armor fasteners, panel seams, and layered muzzle rings require bounded repetition systems.
The open leather saddle, grab hoop, turret shell, and cannon need an action-ready hierarchy with a stable rider socket and non-floating attachments.
Front, profile, three-quarter, and saddle views expose enough of the object to reconstruct the visible systems, while the rear deck and underside remain explicit approximations.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A static box with tracks would fail the layered armor, open saddle, stepped cannon, repeated suspension, and animated mechanical-read contract.

detailInventory.scanMethod: grid-4x4 hero view plus admitted profile, front, and saddle cross-check

definitionOfDone: The tank reads immediately as a compact rideable fantasy tank from front, profile, three-quarter, and gameplay camera views without copying the source name or crest.
The saddle supports the 2.6-yard player rig with a stable seat, grab hoop, clear cannon silhouette, and no visible rider intersection.
Road wheels, track assemblies, suspension, and engine idle carry authored Idle, Walk, Run, and Death clips through the existing mount animation path.
Cream and violet armor, dark tracks, bronze hardware, brown leather, and green textile remain distinct on both Standard and Low-tier materials.
The shipped GLB stays below 14,000 triangles, 576 KiB, 24 primitives, 6 materials, with six embedded procedural maps (two families times albedo, normal, packed ORM) and a live source fingerprint.

Every material carries an independent albedo, roughness, normal, and occlusion response, and the baked macro bands separate each armour plate from the next without crushing the darkest families to black. Verified against the neutral, studio, and grazing-light look-dev renders under docs/screenshots/terrorspark-groundshaker/authoring/material/.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.

screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: The admitted source is a lit stylized illustration rather than a material scan. Palette and response are analyzed per material, and no inferred map from the illustration ships; the maps that DO ship are generated procedurally, per channel, from independent noise fields.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
materialPass.resolutionRationale: World-space box projection makes resolution a texel-density question rather than a UV-island one: at the shipped repeats per yard the albedo runs near 1200 px per yard and the relief fields are band-limited well below their own Nyquist frequency, so a larger map would add bytes and no detail.

mustAvoid: reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The unshown rear engine deck and underside use a restrained functional approximation consistent with the admitted profile and front views.
The source crest, source name, lettering, and exact heraldry are excluded. Shipped armor uses original plain panels and abstract color blocking.
Terrain-conforming tread deformation is out of renderer scope. Baked wheel rotation, tread-loop motion, suspension bounce, and hull motion provide the gameplay movement read.

The shipped World of ClaudeCraft asset uses geometry, vertex colors, and independent scalar material response with zero embedded textures. Source-pixel PBR extraction is intentionally not implementation authority because the reference is a lit illustration, not a material scan.

materials.name: Warm cream painted steel

albedo.samplingNotes: Use the warm cream paint family observed across the glacis and turret, separated from baked highlights.

colorVariation.pattern: semantic vertex color with restrained bevel darkening

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: Projected in world space per triangle from the dominant face-normal axis, so texel density is fixed in yards and never stretches with component scale. UVs are folded to whole repeats per projection group and normalized with KHR_texture_transform so the optimizer can quantize them.

surfaceFrequencyBands.role: ridges, pores, grain, dents, or equivalent visible relief
highlight breakup visible under grazing light

roughness.localResponse: higher roughness in cavities, lower roughness on worn edges

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken creases, seams, intersections, and recessed local features.

localOverrides.region: exposed cream armor bevels and hatch corners
localOverrides.pattern: restrained darker chips and brighter handled edges authored with vertex colors

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Runtime ships procedural PBR maps generated by scripts/assets/terrorspark_groundshaker/surface_maps.mjs (no reference crop or inferred map from the source illustration), plus the semantic vertex zones and the baked macro bands above. Every channel is authored from its own field.

shippedMaps.occlusionRoughnessMetalness: tank_metal_orm, 512 px, R occlusion, G roughness, B metalness; bound as BOTH occlusionTexture and metallicRoughnessTexture
shippedMaps.factorConvention: roughnessFactor and metallicFactor are the authored target divided by the ORM midtone (230/255), so factor times sampled channel equals the target

featureReviews.notes: The full comparison pair preserves the low wide central hull, separated continuous track pods, compact upper mass, and oversized short cannon. The final saddle, layered armor, and surface hierarchy remain assigned to later locked passes.

reviewHistory.summary: The blockout locks the compact tracked-vehicle envelope, central channel, low hull, broad running gear, and dominant cannon before identity detail.
matched: Twin track pods remain wider than the central hull and preserve the front channel.
The short oversized cannon dominates the upper silhouette without becoming a long conventional barrel.
The vehicle reads immediately as a compact rideable tank from front and three-quarter views.
mismatches: Blockout intentionally omits the open saddle, grab hoop, armor layering, tread pads, hubs, hatches, cargo, exhaust, rivets, and final materials.
The blockout turret is lower and cleaner than the final reference hierarchy so rider clearance can be resolved during structural and interaction passes.

visualEvidence.notes: Full vehicle, track separation, cannon projection, hull height, and wheel-bank envelope are visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The simplified blockout deliberately scores only the macro silhouette. Its paired front and hero renders justify advancing to the authored structural hierarchy.

featureReviews.notes: Both continuous track loops, the five-wheel side rhythm, layered hubs, and segmented perimeter pads form one grounded running-gear system without floating parts.
The turret supports a clearly open saddle, rear bolster, grab-hoop arch, mantlet, and cannon root while preserving rider clearance above the hull.

reviewHistory.summary: The complete structural hierarchy now includes twin track loops, ten animated wheel pivots, hull layers, turret, open saddle, grab hoop, mantlet, cannon, cargo, and stable semantic sockets.
matched: Wheel banks are centered inside the tread loops with consistent axle contacts.
The saddle and grab hoop form a readable rideable upper silhouette.
Front, rear, and three-quarter renders show complete volume rather than a camera-facing shell.
mismatches: Structural gray intentionally suppresses the six-material palette and surface wear.
Wheel spokes, upper track skirts, and final form chamfers remain assigned to form refinement.

visualEvidence.notes: Full running gear, cannon hierarchy, saddle opening, grab hoop, rear volume, and contact seams are visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The structural render preserves the reference hierarchy while using an original symbol-free prow and project-authored rear assembly. No child component visibly floats.

featureReviews.notes: The short stepped cannon, low faceted hull, broad continuous tracks, compact turret, saddle, and grab hoop preserve the intended compact fantasy-tank silhouette.
Five spoke-bearing wheels per side, raised hubs, top skirts, segmented pads, and rounded track loops read as one believable running-gear system.
The layered glacis, plain shield prow, turret shoulders, side skirts, hatch-like blocks, and geometric fasteners create the required armor hierarchy without source heraldry.

reviewHistory.summary: Form refinement adds the complete wheel language, upper track skirts, stepped cannon radii, mantlet, deep bore, saddle bolsters, grab hoop, armor overlaps, and bounded hardware.
matched: The cannon remains short and oversized with an unmistakable recessed bore.
Spokes and layered hubs make wheel rotation legible in the animation previews.
The plain shield prow preserves the reference role while excluding its crest.
mismatches: The final model intentionally simplifies tiny dents and scratches into vertex-level value variation rather than fragile micro-geometry.
The rear deck remains a functional project-authored approximation because no rear reference was supplied.

visualEvidence.notes: Silhouette-critical bevels, overlaps, repeated wheel detail, tread segmentation, muzzle depth, saddle opening, and original plain prow are visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The form pass reaches the specified semantic detail inventory without relying on a camera-facing facade. Front, side, rear, and hero views remain coherent.

featureReviews.notes: Warm cream armor, saturated violet plates, near-black iron, bright aged bronze, deep brown leather, and matte forest-green textile remain distinct in hero, front, side, and animation frames.

reviewHistory.summary: The material pass establishes six texture-free semantic materials with vertex color, independent roughness and metalness, strong Low-tier separation, and symbol-free original color blocking.
matched: Cream and violet armor preserve the concept's primary hierarchy.
Dark tread pads, track loops, and cannon separate cleanly from the wheel and hull colors.
Bronze hubs, rivets, collars, and grab hoop provide bounded warm accents.
Leather and forest-green saddle elements remain readable without source textures.
mismatches: The lit illustration is not treated as a physical material scan, so inferred inverse-rendered maps are not embedded or shipped.
Tiny painted scratches are represented by bounded vertex-level variation and real bevel response rather than a copied texture.
codeFixes: Offset tread pads outward to prevent coplanar blending with the continuous belt.
Added original side utility plates, rivets, and a rear exhaust stack to strengthen mechanical locality.

visualEvidence.notes: All six material families, local hardware accents, tread-pad separation, leather saddle, green panels, and exhaust stack are visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The material hierarchy is strongly reference-related but uses no source pixels, lettering, crest, or exact heraldry. The high-contrast semantic palette remains appropriate for gameplay distance.

featureReviews.notes: The side and hero renders preserve material separation while real chamfers, spoke geometry, tread-pad relief, recess depth, and bounded vertex variation break highlights without texture noise.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface review confirms that silhouette-critical relief is real geometry, metal and non-metal responses remain independent, and the texture-free vertex variation avoids flat plastic reads.
matched: Track pads and wheel spokes create tactile relief under angled light.
Bronze hardware catches controlled highlights without turning cream or violet paint into bare metal.
The saddle and green panels remain matte beside the harder armor response.
mismatches: There is no dense scratch texture because the shipping style and Low path rely on geometry, semantic color, and bounded wear.
The review renderer has no dedicated ground plane, so final in-game screenshots must prove contact shadows.

visualEvidence.notes: Track relief, spoke depth, hub layers, armor plates, saddle response, and cannon ring highlights are visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The surface pass uses physically distinct material scalars and actual geometric relief. It deliberately avoids treating a lit illustration as exact PBR source data.

reviewHistory.summary: Neutral key, cool fill, and rear rim lighting preserve cannon depth, track cavities, saddle opening, rear exhaust, and six-material separation without embedded lights or post effects.
matched: The deep muzzle and inner track cavities remain readable instead of crushing to black.
Cream, violet, bronze, leather, textile, and iron stay separated under the neutral authoring rig.
Rear and side views retain complete silhouettes under the same exposure.
mismatches: The generic authoring renderer does not simulate the final world ground shadow or dusk environment.
Final acceptance therefore requires a mounted in-game screenshot under the real renderer.

visualEvidence.notes: Key, fill, rim, dark cavities, material highlights, and silhouette separation are all visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The neutral rig is an evaluation light rather than a copied illustration setup. It exposes form and material errors while keeping the source-related palette recognizable.

featureReviews.notes: The player-scale composite shows a mount-sized saddle above the turret, a protective rear hoop, a clear cannon path, and enough vertical clearance for the 2.6-yard player rig.
Idle, Walk, Run, and Death screenshots resolve live hull motion and ten wheel rotation channels while the rider and exhaust sockets remain extras-bearing empty nodes.

reviewHistory.summary: Interaction review validates player-relative scale, stable rider and exhaust sockets, floor-centered root, ten wheel pivots, four live clips, and a non-breakable semantic hierarchy.
matched: The Tank is broader and slightly taller than the player but remains a compact mount rather than a full-size vehicle.
The saddle and grab hoop are clearly reachable and centered behind the cannon breech.
Walk and Run frames rotate the spoke-bearing wheels while the hull carries controlled suspension motion.
mismatches: Authoring evidence places the player beside the Tank rather than seated on it.
Final seat offset and cannon clearance must therefore be proven in the actual game renderer after catalog integration.

visualEvidence.notes: Tank and 2.6-yard player share one floor line while saddle, hoop, cannon, wheels, and clips remain visible.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The scale and action hierarchy are suitable for a mount. In-game mounted evidence remains a deliberate final acceptance requirement, not an assumption.

featureReviews.notes: Meshopt compression and quantization preserve ten animated wheel nodes, four named live clips, two sockets, all six materials, and the full silhouette in optimized front, side, rear, hero, and clip renders.

matched: Optimized hero, side, rear, and clip renders show no visible quantization or hierarchy regression.
The asset remains below the 14,000 triangle, 24 primitive, and 320 KiB ceilings.
All repeated wheel, tread, hub, rivet, and armor systems remain readable after optimization.

visualEvidence.notes: Optimized geometry, materials, wheel nodes, clips, and semantic silhouettes match the accepted final authoring render.

lightingFromPhoto: Key light: broad warm-white front-left key at 35 degrees elevation and intensity 2.2, separated from the illustrated source lighting.
Fill light: cool broad right fill at intensity 0.8 so tread cavities, saddle opening, and underside armor remain readable.

Review exposure 1.0 with ACES tone mapping, neutral blue-gray background, and soft ground contact shadow under both track loops. Also validate dusk and mobile Low without bloom or dynamic shadows.
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

risks: The source illustration does not expose the complete underside or rear. Restrained functional geometry must be reviewed from rear and low gameplay angles.
